mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility keeps rising from its recent trough, commuting-linked street activity should lift retail visits within four weeks. The effect is strongest when TRANSIT is also stabilizing or improving, because then more workers can physically reach shopping corridors after work.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES increases for at least two consecutive weekly means and TRANSIT is flat or better.

mechanism_narrative: A further fall in RESIDENTIAL time signals more time spent outside home, which directly shifts demand toward shopping and dining trips over the next one to two weeks. The retail effect should reverse if RESIDENTIAL rises again above its current level.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 8.0% and stays there for two weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays at or below its prior 4-week mean after RESIDENTIAL remains below 8.0% for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT continues to improve by at least several points while WORKPLACES remains near current levels, retail mobility should weaken over the next month because fewer people need discretionary trips when commuting normalizes without a corresponding rebound in shopping detours. This mechanism fails if transit recovery is accompanied by a broad consumer reopening.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by 3 or more points week-on-week after a prior decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite a sustained week-on-week rise in TRANSIT without a matching rise in WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rebound in PARKS mobility implies favorable outdoor conditions and more weekend out-of-home activity, which should spill into nearby retail and recreation trips within one week. The signal is strongest when PARKS turns positive after remaining negative in prior weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses from negative to positive week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the following week after PARKS crosses above zero from a negative weekly mean.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM keeps nearing baseline while WORKPLACES stays depressed, households are still making only essential trips and not converting those trips into discretionary shopping. Under that mix, retail mobility should remain lower than the prior four-week average over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last 28-day mean even though GROCERY_PHARM stays near baseline and WORKPLACES remains below -20.

mechanism_narrative: A one-week jump in PARKS combined with lower TRANSIT signals substitution toward local leisure rather than citywide shopping trips. That substitution should pull RETAIL_REC down over the next two weeks because discretionary time is spent outdoors instead of in retail corridors.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises while TRANSIT falls in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days despite PARKS rising and TRANSIT falling in the triggering week.

mechanism_narrative: If mobility restrictions tighten again, the already weak retail level should fall further over the next month because declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES reduce foot traffic into shopping areas. The effect requires both series to soften together; a transit drop alone is not enough.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall for two consecutive weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES post two straight weekly declines.

mechanism_narrative: The recent rise in PARKS from negative territory to positive territory can precede a short-lived retail bounce as people reallocate outings from home to mixed-purpose trips. The effect should appear within one week and fade if PARKS immediately returns below zero.
candidate_trigger: PARKS turns positive after at least two negative weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -8.4 to 7.7 in t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase in the next weekly mean after PARKS turns positive from a multiweek negative spell.
